drugs.moa: Blocks sodium and chloride reabsorption in the loop of Henle, causing rapid, powerful diuresis.
nursing: Give IV slowly to protect hearing
Watch for signs of low potassium
Give early in the day to avoid nighttime urination
teaching: Eat potassium-rich foods (bananas, oranges) unless told otherwise
drugs.tip: Loop & thiazide diuretics WASTE potassium; watch for hypokalemia. Give IV push slowly (ototoxicity).
drugs.pearl: **"Lasix Loses potassium."** Push slow to save the ears.

drugs.moa: Blocks aldosterone, so the body excretes sodium and water while keeping potassium.
nursing: Avoid potassium supplements and salt substitutes
teaching: Report muscle weakness or irregular heartbeat
drugs.tip: Spironolactone SPARES potassium → risk of HYPERkalemia. Opposite of loop/thiazide diuretics.

drugs.moa: Blocks conversion of angiotensin I to II, lowering vasoconstriction and aldosterone → lower blood pressure.
teaching: Report a persistent dry cough or any facial/tongue swelling
drugs.tip: ACE inhibitors (-pril): dry Cough, Angioedema, high potassium (K⁺), Cough. Pregnancy category = avoid.
drugs.pearl: **ACE = "CAPS":** Cough, Angioedema, Pregnancy risk, hyperkalemia (potassium up).

drugs.moa: Blocks angiotensin II at its receptor, causing vasodilation and lower blood pressure — without the bradykinin cough.
nursing: Often used when an ACE inhibitor causes cough
drugs.tip: ARBs (-sartan) are the go-to switch when ACE inhibitors cause a dry cough — no bradykinin, no cough.

drugs.moa: Blocks beta-1 receptors in the heart, lowering heart rate, contractility, and blood pressure.
nursing: Hold and notify provider if HR < 60 or SBP low per parameters
teaching: Diabetics: a fast heartbeat may not warn you of low sugar
drugs.tip: Beta-blockers (-olol): hold if HR < 60. Never stop abruptly (rebound tachycardia/angina). Mask hypoglycemia.
drugs.pearl: **"-olol slows it all."** Check the apical pulse first.

drugs.moa: Increases the force of heart contraction and slows the heart rate.
nursing: Check apical pulse for a full minute; hold if < 60
Assess for toxicity (nausea, anorexia, visual halos)
teaching: Take your pulse before each dose
Report nausea, loss of appetite, or yellow-green vision
drugs.tip: Dig toxicity: nausea, anorexia, yellow-green halos. Low K⁺ raises the risk. Hold if apical HR < 60.
drugs.pearl: **Dig level 0.5–2; hold if pulse < 60.** Antidote = Digibind (Fab).

drugs.moa: Dilates blood vessels (especially veins), reducing cardiac workload and oxygen demand; relieves angina.
drugs.dose: 0.4 mg SL every 5 min x3 for chest pain
nursing: For chest pain: 1 tablet SL, repeat every 5 min up to 3, call 911 if unrelieved
Sit or lie down before taking
Store SL tablets in the original dark bottle
contra: Use of PDE-5 inhibitors (sildenafil) within 24–48 hr
teaching: Sit down before taking (may cause dizziness)
drugs.tip: SL nitro: 1 tab q5min x3, sit down first, expect headache. NEVER with sildenafil (fatal hypotension).
drugs.pearl: **Nitro dilates — sit before you take it.** No ED drugs within 24 hr.

drugs.moa: Blocks cholesterol synthesis in the liver, lowering LDL cholesterol.
nursing: Report unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness
teaching: Report muscle pain or dark urine (rhabdomyolysis)
drugs.tip: Statins: report muscle pain (rhabdomyolysis), watch liver enzymes, avoid grapefruit juice.
drugs.pearl: **Statins → muscle & liver.** Muscle pain + dark urine = stop and report.

drugs.moa: Inhibits vitamin K–dependent clotting factors, preventing new clot formation.
nursing: Keep vitamin K intake (leafy greens) consistent
teaching: Keep green-vegetable intake steady (don't avoid, don't overload)
Use a soft toothbrush and electric razor
Report unusual bleeding or dark stools
drugs.antidote: Vitamin K (phytonadione); FFP/PCC for severe bleed
drugs.tip: Warfarin → monitor INR (goal 2–3), antidote vitamin K. Keep vitamin K foods CONSISTENT, not avoided.
drugs.pearl: **Warfarin = watch INR; antidote vitamin K.** Consistency with greens is the key teaching.

drugs.moa: Activates antithrombin, rapidly inhibiting thrombin and clot formation.
nursing: Never aspirate or massage SC injections
drugs.tip: Heparin → monitor aPTT, antidote protamine. Watch platelets for HIT. Give SC deep, don't rub.
drugs.pearl: **Heparin = aPTT + Protamine.** Warfarin = PT/INR + vitamin K.
